newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ails with Europe as bonds turn sour.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ails with Europe as bonds turn sour.

text.p: Shares fell across the board on Tuesday in moderately active trade, reflecting losses on European bourses, dollar weakness and unrest on the bond and money markets.
The HEX index slumped 1.79 percent to 2199.25, with decliners leading advancers 66-9 and 22 unchanged. Volume was fair at 375 million markka.
Finnish bonds underperformed German bunds and selling was hectic in short maturities.

The bourse index was weighed down by profit-taking in telecoms group Nokia, which fell 8.00 markka to close at 207.50 after rival Swedish Ericsson reported nine-month profits in line with expectations.
Trade in Nokia was lively at over 130 million markka.
Despite the selling pressure on Nokia, analysts said the Ericsson result boded well for the telecoms industry and that they would stand firm by their views of Nokia earnings outlook.
Banking shares softened, with Merita shedding 0.50 markka to end at 13.00, recoiling from recent gains.
"Merita tested the lower end of its trading range, and it is likely to stay within 13 to 15 markka in the near term," one broker said.

Kesko closed 2.70 markka lower at 69.80, extending losses after it announced on Monday plans to divest 40 percent of its Tuko acquisition to win European Union approval for the main portion of the Tuko merger.
Forestries were soft, with UPM-Kymmene shedding 0.30 markka to 93.00 and Enso down 0.70 markka to 35.40, but volumes were unspectacular.
Adding to market jitters was a heavy schedule of U.S. econonomic indicators due later this week.
"It seems that we have hit the bottom for the time being, but uncertainty is likely to persist," one broker said, noting that investors were focused on U.S. October payrolls data due on Friday.
"The market is at a very sensitive stage (after recent gains)," he added.
